title: Sales, costs and profit: thinking like an owner
course_title: Introduction to Small Business and Trading

say: Sales, costs and profit: thinking like an owner.
This is the video for module one of Introduction to Small Business and Trading.

A business is any regular activity where people pay you for something they want, and after all your costs, money is left over. Customers pay because you save them time, effort, transport or worry. That is called creating value.

say: Three words every owner must know. Sales, also called revenue, is all the money customers pay you.

say: Costs are everything you spend to make those sales: the goods, transport, rent, levies and packaging.

say: Profit is sales minus all costs. Always ask yourself, after everything, what did I keep?

say: Here is a worked example. Bisi sells drinks, biscuits and noodles from a table in front of her house in Ibadan. Today her sales add up to about 18,000 naira.

card.title: One day at a provisions table
card.note: Naira figures are illustrative and approximate.

say: Now her costs. The goods she sold cost her about 14,400 naira in cartons. She paid 800 naira for a keke from the market, and 200 naira for nylon bags.

card.title: One day at a provisions table
rows: Cost of the goods she sold
card.note: Naira figures are illustrative and approximate.

say: Total costs, 15,400 naira. So her profit is 18,000 minus 15,400, about 2,600 naira.
She has 18,000 naira in her purse, but only about 2,600 is profit. The 14,400 must go back into stock, or her table will be empty within a week.

say: An owner treats the business as separate from herself. She knows her numbers, pays herself a fixed amount from profit, never touches stock money, and every Sunday asks what went well, what went badly, and what she will change.

panel.heading: Habits that grow a business
right: Takes whatever is in the purse

say: A person who only sells treats the money as household money. If stock money goes on food, school fees or a party, the business shrinks without her noticing.
If you must take money out, write it down.

panel.heading: Habits that grow a business
right: Takes whatever is in the purse

say: Chioma sells rice by the cup in Enugu. A trader offers her a 50 kg bag cheaper. The gain is about 200 naira per kg, or about 10,000 naira on the bag.
The cost is about 85,000 naira at once, and she has 100,000 in business savings.
What could go wrong? Rice stored dry keeps well, so spoilage risk is low.
But spending 85,000 would leave only 15,000 naira for her other goods. So she starts smaller: she shares a bag with a trader she trusts, 25 kg each.
She still saves about 5,000 naira and keeps cash for her other goods. She measured the risk instead of guessing.

panel.heading: Before you spend business money
panel.rule: Measure risk. Never put all your capital into one untested product.

say: Owners write simple rules and keep them. Give credit only to customers who have paid before, with a limit, for example 3,000 naira, and a date to pay.

cards.d: Only to customers who paid before, with a limit, for example ₦3,000, and a date.
Keep cash hidden and bank it or move it to a business account often.
Confirm money has arrived in your own account or POS app. Fake alerts are a known trick.

say: Opportunities hide in complaints, in things people travel far for, and in what families buy every week. Ask people when they last bought, and what they paid, because real past buying tells you more than polite promises.
Halima in Kaduna scored three ideas out of 5. Snacks at the school gate scored 15, the highest, so she tested it with about 25,000 naira of stock and kept the rest as a reserve.

panel.heading: Test demand before you spend
items: Listen to complaints and repeat needs
Ask: when did you last buy, and what did you pay?
Score ideas: demand, start cost, skill, competition

say: To remember. Profit is sales minus all costs, not the cash in your purse. Stock money goes back into stock first. Weigh gain, cost and risk before you spend. Check every transfer in your own app. And test small before you commit your capital.
